source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Electrical, p.6Y-29

procedures.title: Ignition pulse amplifier: disassemble and check components
steps: Resistor R6: use a scale with 150 ohms in or near its middle third; infinite both ways = open.
On reassembly, coat both sides of the flat transistor-to-heat-sink insulators, and the transistor side of the heat sink, with silicone grease (it conducts heat for better cooling).

procedures.title: Spark plugs: clean, regap and install
steps: Clean the plugs thoroughly with an abrasive-type cleaner.
Replace plugs with badly glazed or blistered porcelains.
Use plugs of the same make and number (heat range) in all cylinders.
File the center electrode flat before gapping.
Set the gap to specification with a round feeler gauge, bending only the side (ground) electrode, never the center electrode (see figure 21i in the manual).
Install with new gaskets and torque to specification; without a torque wrench, run them in finger tight and then 1/2 turn more.
Install carefully so the gap is not disturbed.

specs.what: spark plug tightening without torque wrench

procedures.title: Starting motor and solenoid: maintenance
steps: No periodic lubrication or between-overhaul service is needed; the motor and brushes cannot be inspected without disassembly.
notes: On V8s the ignition switch lead to the coil attaches at the coil, not at the starter solenoid as on in-line engines (see figure 2s in the manual).

procedures.title: Starting circuit: resistance check
notes: The starting motor cannot be checked against specifications on the car, but the circuit can be checked for excess resistance.
